newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS END PANTHERS' UNBEATEN STREAK WITH 62 SECONDS TO GO.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS END PANTHERS' UNBEATEN STREAK WITH 62 SECONDS TO GO.

text.p: Joel Otto scored his first goal of the season with 62 seconds left as the Philadelphia Flyers overcame a two-goal deficit and halted the Florida Panthers' season-opening 12-game unbeaten streak with a 3-2 triumph on Saturday.
Trent Klatt passed the puck behind the Florida goal to Otto, who put a wraparound inside the left goal post, beating John Vanbiesbrouck.
Vanbiesbrouck made 41 saves and fell to 6-1-3 as Florida (8-1-4) fell three games short of tying the 1984-85 Edmonton Oilers (12-0-3) for the longest unbeaten streak at the start of a season.
"The mood is pretty sour," said Scott Mellanby, who leads Florida with 12 points. "Losing one game in 13, you wouldn't expect this room to be so down."
"We played their chippy style and played right into their hands," said defenceman Gord Murphy. "This doesn't sit well, to lose like this in our building against a division opponent."
The Flyers have won consecutive games following a three-game losing streak and won for the first time in three meetings with the Panthers this season.
Shjon Podein tied the score 2-2 for Philadelphia with 7:21 left in the third. Klatt's power-play tally had pulled the Flyers within 2-1 with 8:03 left in the second.
Dave Lowry and Ray Sheppard scored for Florida.
In Boston, Wayne Greztky and Alexei Kovalev scored in a 34-second span early in the first period to spark a four-goal outburst as the New York Rangers defeated the Bruins 5-2.

The win extended the Rangers' unbeaten streak to four games (3-0-1) as they reached the .500 level for the first time this season with a 6-6-3 record. Boston fell to 1-4-2 this season at the FleetCenter.
"We've been playing a lot better over the last 10 days, but I still feel we can play much better," said New York captain Mark Messier.
"We're playing much better as a team, as a whole, and defensively, there's no comparison and because of that we've gotten more involved offensively, it's just made a world of difference."
At Colorado, Patrick Roy made 20 saves and Dominik Hasek stopped 32 shots as the Avalanche and Buffalo Sabres fought to a scoreless draw.
The double shutout was the league's second in a week after going nearly 32 months without a scoreless tie. Calgary and Los Angeles played to a 0-0 tie in California last Saturday.
"They are both great goaltenders. When they are focused I'm sure they see the pucks like basketballs," said Sabres captain Pat LaFontaine.
In Vancouver, Trevor Linden and Adrian Aucoin scored 33 seconds apart early in the second period to lead the Canucks to their fourth straight win, 4-3 over the Calgary Flames.

Gino Odjick and the Flames' Sasha Lakovic squared off in the second period and Odjick received minor, major, misconduct and game misconduct penalties, leaving Vancouver shorthanded. But the Canucks still scored less than two minutes later when Linden intercepted a clearing pass, skated in alone and beat Trevor Kidd.

In San Jose, Darren Turcotte's deflection of Jeff Friesen's backhanded pass beat goaltender Jose Theodore and lifted the Sharks to a 4-3 victory over the reeling Montreal Canadiens, who have lost three straight and five of six.
Al Iafrate tied the game for the Sharks with 70 seconds left in regulation.

In Toronto, Sergei Berezin scored twice and fellow rookie Jamie Heward had the first goal and assist of his career as the Maple Leafs beat the Detroit Red Wings for the first time in a year and a half, 6-2.
The Maple Leafs stopped Detroit's current 5-0-2 streak and halted a string of seven straight losses to the Red Wings.

In Hartford, Kevin Stevens, Ed Olczyk and Ray Ferraro each tallied second-period goals and Stephane Fiset stopped all 11 shots he faced in the third period as the Los Angeles Kings held off the Whalers 3-2.

At New Jersey, Dave Andreychuk and Scott Niedermayer capitalised on a four-minute power play with late first-period goals and Martin Brodeur stopped 27 shots as the Devils edged the Tampa Bay Lightning 2-1.
At New York, Ziggy Palffy had two goals and two assists and Derek King scored twice and set up a goal as the Islanders scored a 6-1 victory over the Washington Capitals.
In Pittsburgh, Jaromir Jagr posted his third career hat trick to lead the Penguins to a 7-3 victory over the Ottawa Senators that snapped a four-game losing streak.
